Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for India's reply with the bat to get underway. Roston Chase and Co. take their respective positions on the field. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul to open the innings for the hosts. Jayden Seales will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for West Indies. Seales to Jaiswal. Two slips and a gully in place. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

West Indies will need to come hard at India with the new ball. With Alzarri Joseph and Shamar Joseph unavailable, the onus will fall on Jayden Seales to set the tone. The morning session did offer seam movement with the hard new ball, but batting did seem to become easier once it softened, so India will be wary and look for a steady start. Stick around as India’s reply is coming up right after the break.

Roston Chase and Justin Greaves came together after the break to steady the innings. Greaves impressed with his decisive footwork against spin, something that could well serve as a blueprint for the tourists on this tour. However, even as wickets kept falling around him, his resistance was cut short by Jasprit Bumrah, who delivered a peach of a yorker. Mohammed Siraj had a chance at a maiden five-wicket haul on home soil, but it wasn’t to be, finishing with four scalps as that milestone continues to elude him in Test cricket.

A batting performance the West Indies will be disappointed with. With their innings wrapped up, it is now TEA on Day 1. India, having lost the toss, have done an excellent job to skittle out the opposition in just two sessions. After opting to bat first, it was always going to be a challenge in the opening exchanges. Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj did not hit their straps straight away, but the Windies batters left much to be desired with their shot selection, resulting in the loss of 5 wickets within the first couple of hours.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Kuldeep comes and wraps up the inning of the Windies! Kuldeep bowls a tad shorter, and the line is outside off, getting it across the batter. Jomel Warrican sits down and changes his grip to reverse-sweep it, but misses. The ball brushes his gloves and goes behind the wickets. The keeper, Dhruv Jurel, moves to his right and pouches it. The Indians appeal, and the umpire raises his finger. However, Jomel takes a review, more in hope. The third umpire is called in, and the UltraEdge detects a clear spike when the ball is near the gloves. The on-field decision is upheld, and Kuldeep ends with two wickets. Jomel Warrican walks back for 8 (16), and the Windies get bundled out for just 162 after electing to bat first. And that will be TEA ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Back for the Post-Lunch session! Both umpires walk out again, and so are the players of India. They get into a huddle beside the boundary cushions, led by their skipper, Shubman Gill, who gives a pep talk. Now, they disperse to take their respective positions. Also, stride out the two batters of the West Indies, where the skipper, Roston Chase, will resume the inning alongside a new batter, Justin Greaves. Kuldeep Yadav will complete his unfinished over as he has four balls to bowl. Here we start...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Siraj walked into lunch with 3/19 in 7 overs, Bumrah super tidy with one wicket, and Kuldeep already striking gold. Jadeja and Nitish didn’t find much off the deck yet, which has started to ease out a bit. Right now, it’s India with the momentum, and Windies hanging on with tape. So, what’s next? The second session is basically do-or-die for the West Indies. Can Chase hold his nerve and drag his side past 200 post the Lunch session? Or are we about to see Jadeja and Kuldeep spin a web so tight, it’ll feel like deja vu for Windies collapses in India? The second session will be interesting to see.

Then followed a short fightback of a 48-run stand. Shai Hope, cool as always, linked up with his skipper Chase. The duo decided survival was the move - defending, blocking, nudging. Hope looked the better of the two, playing some crisp strokes, while Chase anchored. For a hot minute, it felt like the West Indies were finally exhaling. But it got turned through Kuldeep Yadav’s entry, who got a big fish, an experienced batter. His eighth ball, Hope bowled! And Windies slipped deeper at 90/5.

Siraj ripped through with absolute precision, first getting Tagenarine Chanderpaul nicking behind down leg for a duck, then Alick Athanaze at second slip and knocking over Brandon King in quick succession. By the way, a special mention to Dhruv Jurel, who has been pretty good behind the stumps, pulling off two sharp takes. Bumrah also chipped in, dismissing John Campbell after a successful review. India were running the show at 42/4 at the end of the first hour, and it was looking like a collapse in disguise.

West Indies' skipper, Roston Chase opted to bat first, hoping the pitch would break down later, but the top order failed to adapt to the early moisture of the deck, which the Indian seamers used to their advantage. Jasprit Bumrah was a bit off at the start, but Mohammed Siraj? The guy came out like where he finished around two months ago in England.

And that will be LUNCH! And if you’re asking who’s ahead right now? Clearly INDIA. Who’s feeling the pressure? Yep, the WINDIES. First session of this 2-match series, and already the gulf looks a bit wide like Wi-Fi signals in a basement. India’s seamers turned the morning into a trial by fire, with the pitch offering that early morning spice. West Indies? They looked unsettled thus far, with a couple of not-so-good shots like Hope tried just at the stroke of Lunch, trying to whack Kuldeep when you are four down already. 90/5 at the break. Yikes!

West Indies (Playing XI) - Tagenarine Chanderpaul, John Campbell, Alick Athanaze, Brandon King, Shai Hope (WK), Roston Chase (C), Justin Greaves, Jomel Warrican, Khary Pierre (On debut), Johann Layne (On debut), Jayden Seales.

The captain of India, Shubman Gill, says that they have 4 Tests at home before the end of this year, and they want to win all 4 games. Shares that the preparation has been good and everyone is in great touch. Adds that it is about switching to the red-ball mindset. Reckons that this is a great surface, but it has been under cover for the past couple of days, so he feels that there might be something in it for the pacers early on. Informs that they have three spinners - Kuldeep Yadav, Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar, with Nitish Kumar Reddy being the seam bowling all-rounder, and the two frontline pacers for this game are Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj.

The West Indies' skipper, Roston Chase, says that his side will bat first. Mentions that the surface looks good, though there is a bit of moisture, and in Test cricket, it will be about surviving that first couple of hours. Notes that it is a young side and the aim is to come out and play positive cricket rather than being timid against India. Points out that batting last here would be difficult as the wicket is expected to turn. Regarding team balance, he explains that the West Indies have opted for two seamers, two spinners, along with an all-rounder, and he himself can also bowl. Further adds that the players have been preparing well, practising sweeps and using their feet, and he hopes they can put those plans into action in this Test.
TOSS - Roston Chase calls it correctly and West Indies have opted to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta and Daren Ganga are pitchside with their thoughts. Speaking on the surface, Ganga first touches on history and reminds that the very first Test played at this venue was against the West Indies in 1983, making this game a bit of a homecoming for the visitors. Explains the uniqueness of the square and highlights the variety of soil types available. To his left, he notes, there are as many as five black-soil pitches, while to his right, red-soil pitches dominate. Mentions that there’s even a mixed surface with both soil types. Adds that the pitch chosen for this game, however, is a red-soil track, which, he points out, binds faster and retains less water. On conditions, Ganga observes that the curator has left an even covering of grass, more than in previous years, giving seamers something to work with. Adds that the overcast skies will enhance swing, not just conventional but also reverse, as the match goes on. Calls it an excellent surface that promises a fierce contest between bat and ball, expecting the turn to come into play later in the Test. Dasgupta then chimes in to agree, noting that it is indeed a red-soil pitch with a healthy grass covering. On touching the surface, he says it feels slightly cold with a bit of moisture present. Concludes that it would not be a surprise if the captain winning the toss opts to bowl first.

The rivalry between these two sides in Tests is heavily stacked in India’s favour, with West Indies’ last win over India coming in 2002. India are still a team in transition, and while they enter the series as favourites, the Windies will be determined to give their best and believe they can achieve a historic result. Neither side has announced its playing XI in the lead-up, and it will be interesting to see how the think tanks read the surface and shape their combinations. Stay tuned for the toss and team news!

For West Indies, Roston Chase’s captaincy chapter could not have begun on a worse note, as he took over from Kraigg Brathwaite ahead of the home series against Australia earlier this year, which they lost 3-0. Brathwaite has been surprisingly left out of this series, leaving Chase and Shai Hope to shoulder the leadership responsibilities. Their pace resources have taken a hit with both Shamar and Alzarri Joseph ruled out through injury, while spin duties will fall on the left-arm duo of Jomel Warrican and Khary Pierre, with Chase himself offering support. With a mix of youth and experience, the Windies will aim to challenge India on their own turf and start this new chapter on a positive note.

The Shubman Gill captaincy era has begun positively with a hard-fought series in England. This will be his first home assignment, while the previous one under Rohit Sharma saw India being handed a drubbing by New Zealand. Much has changed since then, with Rohit, Virat Kohli, and Ravichandran Ashwin retiring. You would have to go back to November 2010 to find a home series without any of the three stalwarts. No surprises in the squad, with Devdutt Padikkal and Axar Patel returning, where Padikkal has been preferred over Karun Nair, who could not make the most of his chances in England. As always, attention will be on Jasprit Bumrah’s workload and whether he features in both Tests.

It all begins here at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad with the first of two Tests against the West Indies, before South Africa arrive later in the year for a full all-format series. The last time the Windies toured India for Tests was back in 2018, when they were comprehensively beaten in both matches.
